title: Carpaccio di tonno
subtitle: Thinly sliced raw tuna with capers, lemon, and olive oil
excerpt: Very thin slices of sushi-grade raw tuna arranged on a plate and dressed with extra-virgin olive oil, lemon juice, capers, and thin-shaved celery. A Sicilian-influenced raw fish antipasto.
sourceNotes: Carpaccio di tonno is a contemporary Italian antipasto that extends the raw-beef carpaccio tradition (created at Harry's Bar, Venice, 1950) to bluefin and yellowfin tuna. It appears in Sicilian and coastal Italian restaurant cooking from the 1980s onwards and is documented in multiple modern Italian antipasto cookbooks including Giorgio Locatelli's Made in Sicily (2011).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tuna can be sliced and arranged on the plates up to 30 minutes ahead, covered with cling film, and refrigerated. Dress just before serving.

glossaryTerms.definition: A trade term indicating that a fish has been handled and frozen (if required) to a standard considered suitable for raw consumption. In the UK, fish sold for raw eating should have been frozen at minus 20°C for 24 hours to kill any parasites, or sourced from a supplier with appropriate handling certification. Ask your fishmonger.

content.text: tuna: fish that has been handled to a standard suitable for raw eating. Ask your fishmonger for this specifically; do not use supermarket tuna steaks unless they are labelled for raw consumption. Given the right fish, this is one of the quickest and most impressive antipasti you can make: a few minutes of slicing and arranging, a simple dressing, and it is done.

items.prepNote: sushi-grade yellowfin or bluefin, in a single piece
pale inner sticks with leaves, very thinly sliced

content.text: Place the tuna in the freezer for 20 to 30 minutes until very firm but not frozen solid. This makes slicing easier and produces cleaner, thinner slices.
Using a very sharp, thin-bladed knife, slice the tuna as thinly as possible, about 2 to 3 mm. Arrange the slices on four cold plates, overlapping them slightly to cover the base of each plate.

Mix the olive oil and lemon juice together and drizzle over the tuna. Scatter capers, thin celery slices, celery leaves, and parsley over the top. Season with sea salt flakes and black pepper. Serve immediately, or cover with cling film and refrigerate for up to 30 minutes before dressing.

items.symptom: Tuna is ragged and tears when sliced
items.cause: Not cold enough, or knife not sharp enough
items.fix: The tuna must be very firm from the freezer. A sharp, flexible-bladed knife is essential.
Carpaccio needs generous seasoning with salt and enough lemon juice to cut through the fat of the fish. Season each plate just before serving.

content.text: Raw tuna carpaccio is a dish of the Sicilian coast and the Italian Adriatic. It appears in the high-end restaurants of Palermo and Taormina and in the simpler trattorie of the Sicilian fishing ports, where fresh bluefin tuna is landed. Raw tuna, capers (a Sicilian staple from the island of Pantelleria), olive oil, and lemon is a classic Sicilian flavour profile. It works just as well in a London or Sydney kitchen when the right fish is available.
